_comment: Cairn's register, and the ONLY hand-written list in the project.
It is hand-written because a designation is a speech act, not a fact about
the filesystem. Trevor assigns one by saying it; nothing on disk knows it
happened, and no amount of derivation will find a session that never
committed anything. Everything Cairn does around this file is derived.
THE CENSUS THAT SETTLED THAT. Extracting designations from prose by shape
found 463 candidates across 175 docs -- Challenge 1, Job 6, Set 2, Day 1,
Aurora Beam 50, UT 92 -- with the real ones a small minority buried inside.
Marquee has a scar about exactly this shape of mistake: a grep for authored
defects flagged 13 of 18 games, reporting the opposite of the truth, and it
passed every assertion. So designations are DECLARED here or they stay
unknown. Do not add a cleverer regex.
WHAT EACH FIELD IS FOR
designation  the canonical form, always '<Prefix> <number>'.
signature    how it actually appears, when that differs. CTown-4 and
CTown-5 carry a hyphen because they are among the first ever
issued and the format had not settled. Recorded as written,
never normalised -- the same reason 041 keeps its name.
state        closed (default) | open | never. See below.
signed       where this session put its name, as a QUOTE rather than a
line number. Cairn checks each quote is still in the file it
names, so a credit that gets edited away is reported. Line
numbers drift with every edit; a quote only stops matching
when the credit itself changes.
THREE STATES, AND WHY 'ABSENT' IS NOT ONE OF THEM
open   the session has not finished. CTown 3 is paused waiting on data
from outside the tree for a job that belongs to somebody else, and
will pick back up. Having no commits yet is work in progress here,
not a hole in the record, and the two must never render alike.
never  the number does not name anybody and deliberately never will. This
row exists so that nobody fills the gap in, and so that nobody
renumbers around it. It is the 'assert the deliberate properties'
rule from building.md, in data.
SHORTHAND. Inside its own folder a session may sign just '#30'; the folder
supplies the rest. So Shadowless #30 is Shadowless 30, and a number alone
is meaningless across collections -- KSP 1 and Shadowless 1 are different
people. Work done from outside the folder uses the full designation.
WHAT IS NOT IN HERE YET, deliberately. Shadowless has numbered its sessions
to #33 in LOGBOOK-*.md and GRABHIST-*.md under headings of a rigid shape
('## #30 -- Opus 5, 29 Aug 2026 (...)'). That is a structured key rather
than prose, so it can be DERIVED, and transcribing 33 rows by hand here
would be a second copy that drifts the moment #34 lands. It is pass 2 and
it is a derivation, not a transcription. The project is also under a
maintenance freeze, which is a second reason not to reach into it.
